questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: First of all, it was important for me, that the country i was going to stay in, was an english speaking country. Secondly, i knew that australia was an amazing place, due to prior travelling.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was decently easy - the exchange student advisor at USYD was great at responding to emails quickly, and overall she provided all the necessary information regarding the important dates and other important reminders.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The student advisor at USYD.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Flatmate is a great place to find housing, and so is gumtree. I recommend starting the process as early as possible as it was incredibly competitive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Its great, but be prepared to spend a long time in public transport if you have classes that cant be attended online.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You had to send multiple emails to the student advisor in order for you to get your student ID, but once you had that it was smooth sailing.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Again, the student advisor assigned to exchange students was great.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure to get there in time for the introduction week, very helpful for teaching you how to find you way around the campus and they tell you all that needs to be done for the registration.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took three third year courses relevant to my degree, and they were all great. The lecturers and the lectures themselves were interesting. There was a fair bit of overlap with courses i had previously taken at UCPH. Expect to spend a significant amount of time on assignments and other school related tasks.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Teaching is very similar, except for the fact that multiple assignments needed to be completed as part of the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
BCMB3003, Biochemistry of Human Disease,
BCMB3004, Beyond the Genome
CHEM3121, Chemical Biology
EDUH4052, Learning in Outdoor Education

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
If you have an interest in chemistry and biology CHEM3121 is a great course. Dont take this course unless you have done second year chemistry already though. 
BCMB3004 was also great - Stuart, the lecturer, was incredibly passionate and intelligent, making the class very interesting. Also the stuff we were taught was very cutting-edge, making it even more interesting. Lab in this course is a bit subpar though. 
For learning about Australia itself i recommend EDUH4052. This course will teach you about the Australian environment and nature, and take you on two gorgeous trips to the Blue Mountains and the Royal National Park, which was a great way to explore and meet other exchange students.

questions.answer:
Some courses require you to pay an extra amount (EDUH4052 requires a fee in order to participate in the field trips)
Drinking a lot with other exchange students quickly becomes expensive:)

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Prices in Sydney are generally speaking similar to Copenhagen, so nothing too out of the ordinary. Smoking is incredibly expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Millions upon millions of different clubs, that all seemed fun.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: SURFING!! Renting a car and driving around the coast. Eating well. Parachuting.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Again, drive up and down the coast. Its a great way to explore the country. Sydney is also massive, so make sure to explore most of it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, very western culture in Australia.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Say hi and dont be a prick.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The focus on being outdoors all the time was very refreshing. In Bondi, where i lived, everyone was fit, ate well and spent all their time in the sun, which was something i quite enjoyed being a part of.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Dont focus too much on school, and enjoy that you are on exchange. 
Dont enroll yourself into multiple challenging courses - instead i recommend doing random courses that you think might be fun or interesting. There is no shame in doing a first year course in something new, just because you think it sounds fun (unless you truly are there for studying and not for the experience)
Make sure to start socializing early, as having a group of friends greatly enhances the experience and reduces stress.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Cant think of any

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Spending time getting to know new people and exploring the vast nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The start of the exchange was by far the hardest - You're alone, with no place to live, no friends or family. You're on your own, which can be intimidating and stressfull. However, it was also incredibly rewarding to overcome this, and i definitely dont think that this is something that should withhold you from doing an exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
